stem: In the equation \(|x^{2} - 6x| = k\), \(k\) is a constant. If the equation has exactly 3 distinct real solutions, what is the value of \(k\)?
solution: The graph of \(y = x^{2} - 6x\) is a parabola with \(x\)-intercepts 0 and 6 and vertex \((3, -9)\).

Taking the absolute value reflects the part below the \(x\)-axis upward, so the graph of \(y = |x^{2} - 6x|\) touches the \(x\)-axis at \(x = 0\) and \(x = 6\) and has a peak at \((3, 9)\) between them.
A horizontal line \(y = k\) meets this graph at exactly 3 points only when it passes through the peak, so \(k = 9\).

explanation.A: Correct. The line \(y = 9\) passes through the peak \((3, 9)\) and crosses the outer parts of the graph twice, for 3 solutions in all.
explanation.B: Incorrect. With \(k = 0\), the equation is equivalent to \(x^{2} - 6x = 0\), which has only 2 solutions, 0 and 6.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex, not the value of \(k\). With \(k = 3\), the equation has 4 solutions.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the nonzero \(x\)-intercept of \(y = x^{2} - 6x\), not the value of \(k\). With \(k = 6\), the equation has 4 solutions.
